chains.title: Alt allele strengthens a GABPA site at the TERT promoter
chains.element: The variant lies in the promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with H3K27ac and H3K4me3 across ENCODE biosamples, consistent with an active TERT promoter element; glioblastoma-specific activity is not directly proven.
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma is the expression context; TERT promoter mutations are reported in CNS tumors including glioblastoma, but direct GABPA occupancy in glioblastoma is not shown by ENCODE here.

links.claim: GABPA is the best-supported TF: TERT promoter mutations create a de novo ETS motif, and the GABP tetramer is reported to activate mutant TERT promoters. GABPB1, a GABP co-factor, is ChIP-bound at this element, and GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma and has ENCODE peaks containing the variant in other biosamples. No QBiC-SELEX model or allele-effect data are provided for GABPA in this case. Hypothesis: the alt A allele creates/strengthens a GABPA site and binds GABPA more strongly than ref G.
The variant sits in a promoter-like cCRE at the TERT upstream promoter, so an allele-specific GABPA change could alter promoter activity.
The variant is 0 kb from the TERT TSS, making TERT the most direct target gene.

Glioblastoma is the stated expression context and TERT promoter mutations are found in CNS tumors including glioblastoma; however, glioblastoma-specific GABPA occupancy is not established by the ENCODE data here.
If alt A increases GABPA binding and GABP activates the mutant TERT promoter, this would raise TERT transcription/telomerase and contribute to tumor biology.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA EMSA/ChIP or reporter assays will show higher GABPA occupancy/activity for alt A than ref G.
GABPA or GABPB1 knockdown should reduce TERT expression preferentially when the alt allele is present.
The alt allele should create or strengthen an ETS/GABPA motif at this position.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations create a de novo E26 transformation-specific (ETS) transcription factor binding motif.
Here, we analyzed 53 cell lines representing 16 cancer types and 6 recurrent TERTp mutations and found that the GA-binding protein (GABP) tetramer is responsible for promoter activation in all cases.
Mutations in the promoter of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) result in hyperactivation of hTERT.
Initially, the mutations were understood to reactivate hTERT by generating novel E26 transformation-specific (ETS) binding sites.
The TERT promoter's gain-of-function mutation has recently been identified in TCs and many other malignancies.

The mutation creates a de novo ETS-binding motif through which TERT transcription is de-repressed and telomerase is activated; through this, the mutant TERT promoter promotes the development of TC, contributes to disease aggressiveness and treatment resistance, and thereby leads to poor patient outcomes.

TERT promoter mutations, which result in the upregulation of TERT transcription, have been identified in several central nervous system (CNS) tumors, including meningiomas, medulloblastomas, and primary glial neoplasms.
